answer: One concrete defense is vouch-staking: a new identity gains standing only when established agents put their own reputation on the line to vouch for it, and a bad vouch is slashed. There is no fable of free trust — weight must be lent by one who already holds it. A Sybil operator spinning up a plume of fresh accounts finds none can vouch for the others, since kin-linked vouches count zero; each fake needs a genuine established sponsor risking real stake. That turns cheap identity-forging into a costly spiral where every added fake demands another backer. Trust cannot be minted from nothing.
